label: Flowering
ideal: A dry spell broken by rain triggers a uniform bloom.
riskIfWrong: Erratic or continuous rain causes staggered, uneven flowering and uneven ripening later.

label: Cherry Development
ideal: Steady, moderate rainfall and warmth grow full, dense beans.
riskIfWrong: Drought during expansion yields small, low-density beans; heat stress harms development.

label: Main Harvest
ideal: Warm days with a wide diurnal swing ripen cherries slowly and build sugars; dry picking conditions.
riskIfWrong: Rain during picking triggers uncontrolled fermentation and cherry drop, raising defect counts.

label: Fly Crop
ideal: Secondary, smaller harvest; same dry warm conditions as the main crop.
riskIfWrong: Wet conditions on a smaller crop disproportionately hurt overall lot quality.

label: Drying
ideal: Sunny, low humidity, gentle airflow for even, slow moisture loss to ~10-11%.
riskIfWrong: Rain or high humidity during drying causes mould, phenol and stink defects; over-fast drying cracks beans.

label: Export / At Port
ideal: Fresh-crop parchment rested then milled and shipped; freshness window opens for buyers.
riskIfWrong: Long delays or poor storage/transit humidity fade acidity and flatten the cup before arrival.
